builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
summary: The method replaces training and maintaining separate models per inference budget with one mixture-of-experts model that reuses parameters through pre-defined looped execution paths at five depths. It costs joint pretraining on 3.6T tokens plus budget-aware SFT, RL, parameter-group merging, and multi-teacher distillation, which is far beyond a 24 GB GPU and limited cloud budget. If adopted only as an inference idea on non-Accordion weights it fails, because the elastic budgets exist only in models specifically pretrained and fine-tuned for layer looping.
rationale: The gains depend on a pretrained Accordion checkpoint, so a constrained team cannot reproduce them and can only benefit if the authors release compatible weights.
technique: Elastic-depth inference via fixed-prefix layer looping

claims.statement: The method replaces training and maintaining separate models per inference budget with one mixture-of-experts model that reuses parameters through pre-defined looped execution paths at five depths. It costs joint pretraining on 3.6T tokens plus budget-aware SFT, RL, parameter-group merging, and multi-teacher distillation, which is far beyond a 24 GB GPU and limited cloud budget. If adopted only as an inference idea on non-Accordion weights it fails, because the elastic budgets exist only in models specifically pretrained and fine-tuned for layer looping.

After 3.6T tokens of pretraining, increasing inference depth improves Accordion-6B-A0.5B's five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points, with the middle budget capturing 89% of this gain using half as many additional layer executions.
